title: Momoni: a privacy-first personal finance product
headline: From blank page to daily use in two weeks, without sending anyone's finances to the cloud
summary: A desktop finance app that turns bank statements, receipts and chat messages into a monthly plan, while every rupiah of personal data stays on the user's own computer.
role: Product owner, UX/UI designer, architect, engineer

context: Young professionals in Indonesia pay by credit card, QRIS, e-wallet and cash. Spending ends up in five places, and budgeting apps either want bank credentials or upload everything to their own servers.
The brief I set myself: one place for every rupiah, built so that the most sensitive data never has to leave the user's laptop.

approach.title: Privacy by architecture, not policy
approach.body: The database is encrypted on the device and its keys live in the operating system's keystore. The cloud only relays new entries and stores backups it cannot read.

approach.title: Meet the user where money moves
approach.body: Credit card statement PDFs are parsed automatically, QRIS receipts arrive from an iPhone shortcut, and purchases can be logged by chatting with a Telegram bot ("coffee 25k").

approach.title: From tracking to decisions
approach.body: A pay-yourself-first plan splits each payday into fixed costs, emergency fund, retirement and goals, and turns what is left into a daily "safe to spend" figure.

approach.title: Staged delivery with an AI pair
approach.body: I wrote the specification as 20 numbered stages with explicit quality and security gates. AI accelerated implementation; I owned the architecture, the security review and the QA sign-off at every stage.

design.intro: I designed every screen before it was built, explored several directions on a design canvas, and wrote each decision down with the reason, so the build could follow it without guessing.

points.title: One number first
points.body: The dashboard opens with a single sentence from Momo and the figure people actually ask for: how much is still safe to spend today. Flow and Calendar sit one tab away for when they want the detail.

points.title: Statement check as a merge
points.body: A BCA statement is compared with what Momoni already recorded, like reviewing a pull request: every difference must be resolved before the month can be saved, so totals always match the bank to the rupiah.

points.title: Honest budget pace
points.body: Instead of a blanket "budget safe", the budget shows what is left per day including today, and a plain status: on track, spending fast, almost out, or over.

points.title: The app suggests, the user decides
points.body: The payday plan proposes how to split income, but nothing changes until the user applies it, with undo. Momoni never moves money: the user transfers it and ticks it off.

points.title: Four ways to see categories
points.body: A list, a treemap, columns and a drag-and-drop board replace a single tree, and each person picks the view the page opens with.

points.title: Wealth in plain language
points.body: Terms like "capital invested" and "unrealised gain", a reminder when an asset's value is more than 30 days old, and goals funded by allocating amounts from real assets.

brand.title: From Dompi to Momoni
story: The product started as Dompi, a wallet logo in solid orange. As the app grew from a tracker into something people check every day, it needed a character rather than an icon. Momoni is built around Momo, a tuxedo cat based on a real cat near my house who shows up every morning asking for food. That habit is the idea: Momo shows up every day and reminds you to check on your money.
The new mark keeps the wallet, so the change reads as an evolution: Momo peeks out of it with white paws on the edge.

lockup.label: Lockup · Plus Jakarta Sans 800

brand.paletteNote: Dompi was orange everywhere. Momoni takes Momo's black and white as the base and keeps orange as a 6% accent. Text on orange is always ink (6.1:1); white on orange fails contrast.
brand.expressionsNote: Momo never jokes about a problem with someone's money: errors use the worried face with plain, helpful copy.

productPage.title: See Momoni the way a user would
productPage.body: An interactive product page: try the Telegram bot, drop a statement, split a payday and work out your own safe number. Everything runs in the browser on invented data.

impact.title: In daily use
impact.body: Running on real personal finances since the first release, with the data carried safely through a full platform rewrite.

impact.title: Re-platformed for speed
impact.body: Moving from a Java + embedded PostgreSQL desktop to an in-process Rust core in Tauri cut cold start from 6.9 s to 0.3 s, install size from 254 MB to 16 MB, and memory from 833 MB to 439 MB.

impact.title: Built to keep growing
impact.body: A private project I keep developing, against a staged roadmap that runs from storage and security foundations to importing statements from more banks.

title: An internal platform for AI training workflows
headline: Designing a backend from scratch and tuning search so teams find the right training data
summary: Designed and built an internal web platform supporting AI training workflows, with about ten REST endpoints and tuned Elasticsearch relevance.
context: Research teams needed an internal web platform to support their AI training workflows, built alongside frontend engineers in an Agile team.

approach.title: API design from a blank page
approach.body: Built about ten RESTful endpoints from scratch in Java using an MVC structure and clear DTO layers.

approach.title: Search that finds the right data
approach.body: Implemented and fine-tuned Elasticsearch indexing and relevance scoring.

approach.title: Consistent environments
approach.body: Containerised services with Docker and modelled the database interactions the frontend relied on.

impact.title: Better retrieval
impact.body: Improved search accuracy and data retrieval performance for training data.

impact.title: Maintainable codebase
impact.body: Reduced cognitive complexity and code smells flagged by static analysis, delivered iteratively with Jira and Kanban.

title: Teaching Java to 500+ students in a national upskilling programme
tileTitle: Teaching Java in a national upskilling programme
headline: Turning beginners into job-ready programmers through structured, hands-on curriculum
summary: Delivered Java programming training to more than 500 students as part of Indonesia's national upskilling programme, and designed the curriculum behind it.
context: Indonesia's national upskilling programme aimed to prepare people for programming jobs. Many students arrived with no programming background.

approach.title: Structured curriculum
approach.body: Designed a structured curriculum that builds from fundamentals to complete applications.

approach.title: Learning by building
approach.body: Hands-on projects aimed at what employers expect from a junior developer.

impact.title: 500+ students trained
impact.body: Delivered Java training to more than 500 students across the programme.
